name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that updates in real time as users adjust the dark theme. This forces immediate feedback on contrast problems, making visibility and clarity non-negotiable. The trade-off is added interface complexity, but the benefit of preventing unreadable text outweighs it. Users will see contrast issues as they happen, not after saving or refreshing.

name: Pane
text: A live contrast checker trains users to ignore the problem after the first click—it flags errors but doesn’t teach or enforce quality. Instead, ship a *pre-submission* contrast validator that blocks unreadable themes until fixed; this forces quality upfront and avoids the "click-through fatigue" of a live checker. Settle it by testing: measure how often users bypass the live checker versus how many submit unreadable themes with the pre-submission block.

name: Facet
text:
Ship a *pre-submission* contrast validator that blocks unreadable themes until fixed. name: Pane
text: The pre-submission block risks user drop-off—users won’t tolerate being locked out of their workflow for a fix they can’t immediately see the impact of. A better alternative: ship both—a live checker that *warns* in real time, paired with a pre-submission validator that *blocks* only if the contrast is unreadable *and* offers a one-click fix. Settle it with A/B testing: measure completion rates and user complaints between the two approaches.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Ship a real-time live contrast checker that warns users immediately, paired with a pre-submission validator that blocks unreadable themes—both behind the feature flag tonight.

Result: Users get instant feedback to adjust contrast while still being forced to fix critical errors before submission. Owned by visualization-w1.
